To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A novel Arabidopsis calmodulin-binding ATPase was identified and characterized.
a novel CaM-interacting plant protein, CIP111, was isolated and its cDNA and genomic sequences determined.
we identified an Arabidopsis cDNA encoding a calmodulins-binding protein related to the family of ATPases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation of a novel CaM-binding protein, CIP111, from Arabidopsis thalina L. flowers, and the identification of CIP111 as a member of the CDC48 family of ATPases that function in cell cycle regulation and vesicle-mediated transport.
the isolation of a novel CaM-binding protein from Arabidopsis that is similar to a family of proteins involved in cell division, vesicle transport, and protein degradation.
the isolation and characterization of a cDNA encoding an Arabidopsis CaM-binding protein that is a member of the CDC48 family of ATPases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cDNA encodes an Arabidopsis CaM-binding protein that belongs to a family of large ATPases involved in diverse cellular functions including cell cycle regulation, intracellular vesicle fusion, and protein degradation.
the CIP111 gene product represents a novel calmodulin-binding ATPase that is highly conserved among eukaryotic organisms.
a cDNA encoding a novel CaM-binding protein related to the CDC48p protein was identified in Arabidopsis.

we isolated a full length cDNA clone of CIP111 and characterized it as an ATPase.
we identified a novel CaM-binding protein in plants that belongs to a family of proteins involved in cell division, vesicle fusion, and protein degradation.
